correctness.rationale: For regular Euclidean 2n-gon B_n and its polar B_n*, convexity in both primal arguments permits maxima at vertices. Dualizing N(x+ty)+N(x-ty) gives (1/2)max_{f,g in B_n*}[N*(f+g)+tN*(f-g)]. The polar vertices w_j=sec(beta)(cos((2j+1)beta),sin((2j+1)beta)), beta=pi/(2n), are an isometric rotated-scaled copy of primal regular vertices; dihedral symmetry reduces to angular differences 0<=j<=n. Chord norms are exactly 2 q_j cos(j beta) and 2 q_{n-j} sin(j beta) with q even=1, odd=sec beta, giving the stated finite affine envelope for all real t>=0. Since each maximizing dual vertex pair has equal Euclidean length, w_i+w_j perpendicular to w_i-w_j; choosing primal support endpoints for their perpendicular direction pair gives the same symmetric orbit (v_0,v_floor(n/2)) as an optimizer at every t, including zero-vector degenerate choices. Independently enumerated all 2n primal vertex competitors versus fixed pair and envelope for n=2..150 at 13 scales without disagreement (corroboration only). For n=5 the exact four undominated lines and their golden-ratio intersections yield rho(1)=(3sqrt5-5)/4. The mathematical proof is all n/t, not extrapolated from samples.
